reason: The measurements are largely right and the boundary mismatch is real (geometry at 701, composition at 1024), but the finding misattributes the harm and its own fix does not deliver the benefit it claims. Measured owner-flight across 390/700/701/768/834/900/1023/1024: first moment y=967 at 701/768/834, y=937 at 900/1023, y=570 at 1024; doc height 2527 / 2497 / 2130; ownerScale 18px/day from 701. So far so accurate. But: (1) THE FIX DOES NOT WORK AT ITS OWN HEADLINE WIDTH. I simulated the exact proposal - the [data-medium="full"] half of the 701 raise neutralised below 1024, plus ownerScale at 14px/day. The first moment lands at y=839 (768), y=809 (900 and 1023). Not 'roughly y=790', and still BELOW the 800px fold. Side-by-side screenshots at 1023x800 before and after are the same screen: counter, date, today rule, gap note, empty rail, no moment. The fix shrinks the type and changes nothing the finding says it fixes. (2) THE 282px EMPTY RAIL IS NOT A BAND DEFECT. Origin-to-first-tick is 288px at 1023 and 288px at 1024, 1152, 1280 and 1440 alike. It is the ratified time-proportional rail carrying a real 16-day gap with its own gap note, identical in the band round 7 just fixed. Charging it to 701-1023 is wrong. (3) THE DEAD FIELD CLAIM INVERTS. At 768 the item is 452px and the title 452px - zero dead field; at 834, 518/518 - zero dead field. Those are the iPad-portrait widths the finding names as the harm. Only at 1023 is there slack (title caps at 544 inside a 707px item), and under the proposed fix that slack gets WORSE, not better: 721-544 = 177px against 163px today, because the title cap is 544 either way and phone geometry moves the row 14px further left. The fix makes the one number it could have improved worse. (4) THE iPAD CASE IS FALSE AS STATED. iPad portrait is 768x1024 and 834x1112, not 768x800. At 768x1024 the first moment's title renders at y=967-996, above the fold today; the fix is not needed there and would cost it, dropping 24px titles to 17px on a 576px measure that currently has no dead field at all - a phone counter and a phone date stretched across a tablet, which is the very defect the finding is named after. (5) 'Graded by nothing at all' is overstated: 768 is asserted in seven loops of interaction-check.mjs (204, 301, 566, 949, 980, 1233, 1321) and 1023 in the docked-sheet measure loop at 2492. What is left after all that is one narrow true case - a non-maximised ~900-1023px desktop window at 800px tall, where no moment is above the fold - and the proposed fix does not solve it (y=809). Solving it would mean cutting the horizon block's height or the gap the rail honestly draws, both ratified decisions, not moving a media boundary. Refuted: the fix is measurably inert at the width it targets, regresses the width it claims to protect, and two of its three supporting numbers belong to the composition at every desk width rather than to this band.
